q-33972.name: Question 1
q-33972.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨2,4,-1⟩+t⟨1,4,3⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨3,12,9⟩=45.
$$
q-33972.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨2+t,4+4t,-1+3t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨2+t,4+4t,-1+3t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,12,9⟩ & =45 \\ ⟨2+t,4+4t,-1+3t⟩\cdot ⟨3,12,9⟩ & =45 \\ 3(2+t)+12(4+4t)+9(-1+3t) & =45 \\ 6+3t+48+48t-9+27t & =45 \\ 78t & =0 \\ t & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=0$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨2+(0),4+4(0),-1+3(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,4,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(2,4,-1).$

q-108308.name: Question 4
q-108308.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨-1,2,1⟩+t⟨3,0,2⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩=13.
$$
q-108308.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =13 \\ ⟨-1+3t,2,1+2t⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,2⟩ & =13 \\ 1(-1+3t)-2+2(1+2t) & =13 \\ -1+3t-2+2+4t & =13 \\ 7t & =14 \\ t & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-1+3(2),2,1+2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨5,2,5⟩\end{aligned}

q-108434.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,-1,2⟩+w⟨3,4,-1⟩,\,Π:r=⟨5,3,-4⟩+s⟨1,0,2⟩+t⟨0,-2,3⟩.
$$
q-108434.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨1,0,2⟩\times ⟨0,-2,3⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =4i-3j-2k \\  & =⟨4,-3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =⟨5,3,-4⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1,-1,2⟩+w⟨3,4,-1⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19 \\ ⟨1+3w,-1+4w,2-w⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19 \\ 4(1+3w)-3(-1+4w)-2(2-w) & =19 \\ 4+12w+3-12w-4+2w & =19 \\ 2w & =16 \\ w & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=8$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨1+3(8),-1+4(8),2-8⟩ \\  & =⟨25,31,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(25,31,-6).$

q-108891.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\frac{x+2}{3}=\frac{y}{4}=\frac{1-z}{2},\,Π:r\cdot ⟨4,-3,1⟩=-9.
$$
q-108891.worked_solution:
From the equation of the line $l$, we know that it passes through the point $A(-2,0,1)$ and it is parallel to the vector $v=⟨3,4,-2⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨-2,0,1⟩+t⟨3,4,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2+3t,4t,1-2t⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Now, substituting $r=⟨-2+3t,4t,1-2t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,1⟩ & =-9 \\ ⟨-2+3t,4t,1-2t⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,1⟩ & =-9 \\ 4(-2+3t)-3(4t)+(1-2t) & =-9 \\ -8+12t-12t+1-2t & =-9 \\ -2t & =-2 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨-2+3(1),4(1),1-2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,4,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get $P(1,4,-1).$
